clue.text: It's about a pound in English money

definitions.text: It's about a pound in English money

parts.words: It's about a pound in English money
parts.note: the Latin motto lettered around the rim of the British pound coin, so it literally runs about the coin

explanation.surface: Someone explaining the worth of something as roughly a pound sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'approximately' but means 'around the edge of': the motto, Latin for 'an ornament and a safeguard', is inscribed on the edge of the UK one-pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase is the edge inscription on British pound coins, literally running around the money.

clue.text: Tossed coin, side creating government policy?

indicators.note: a tossed coin is thrown about, so the letters of the next words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: creating means making

explanation.surface: Deciding a matter of state by flipping a coin and taking a side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossed coin' looks like part of the picture, but 'Tossed' is the anagram signal; the question mark admits that government is only loosely a matter of making choices.
explanation.definitionFit: Government is, loosely and with a question mark, the business of reaching choices on policy: a process of choosing.

clue.text: Vehicle capacity causes state highway to switch sides

indicators.note: the sides are left and right, so the L and R letters trade places

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
a highway is a road

explanation.surface: Traffic changes lanes on a state highway, affecting how much a vehicle carries.
explanation.walkthrough: CAL + ROAD gives CALROAD; 'to switch sides' swaps L (left) and R (right), giving CARLOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A carload is the amount a car can carry, its full capacity of goods or passengers.

clue.text: Short Australian social could become lustful

indicators.note: says the letters may turn into something else once rearranged

parts.note: Aus is the shortened form of Australian

explanation.surface: A brief Australian get-together might turn into something racy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' rearranges AUS plus SOCIAL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Salacious describes lewd, lecherous behaviour, a close synonym of lustful.

clue.text: A lintel may take time to redeem

parts.note: to ransom someone is to redeem them by payment

explanation.surface: A builder says fitting a lintel may take a long time to set right.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar above a door or window, i.e. a lintel.

clue.text: Note work by Scot is ideal

parts.note: ut is the old name for the note now called doh
op (opus) is a musical work
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A note composed by a Scottish musician is perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian means perfect or visionary, as in an idealised society, so it matches ideal.

clue.text: Suit one lost in London

indicators.note: says a piece goes missing from the word before

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lawsuit falls apart in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is legal, not clothing: ACTION loses I to leave ACTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a district of west London, so the phrase locating it is a place definition.

clue.text: Time for this clue starting off with gin sling?

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the word before

parts.note: this clue is numbered 7, so it stands for seven

indicators.note: a gin sling is a drink, but to sling is to fling about, so the letters of gin are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to begin the night's drinking with a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is 7-down, so 'this clue' is SEVEN; 'starting off' drops S to give EVEN, and 'sling' rearranges GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening is a time of day, the hours after work when a gin sling might be poured.

clue.text: Agreement with composer for playing in a quartet?

parts.note: a contract is a formal agreement
Frank Bridge was an English composer

explanation.surface: A deal signed with a composer to perform in a string quartet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'quartet' suggests a string quartet, but it is the four players at the card table; Frank Bridge was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is a card game played by four people in two partnerships, hence playing in a foursome.

clue.text: All or nothing about turning feature of flower

indicators.note: says the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: An all-or-nothing remark about a flower turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the whole string ALLOROC, giving COROLLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The corolla is the ring of petals of a flower, one of its main parts.

clue.text: Active in the Goon Show

indicators.note: a show is a display or production, so the letters are put on show in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lively in the classic radio comedy The Goon Show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s BBC radio comedy; 'Show' rearranges THE GOON into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being constantly busy and moving about is to be active.

clue.text: One resigned when about to get endlessly ill

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes around the short word next to it
the last letter is taken off

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone who gave up a post just as illness was setting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SICK to SIC, which goes 'about' TO to make S-TO-IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic accepts hardship without complaint, being resigned to fate.

clue.text: One might study insects, it could be

indicators.note: says the letters might turn into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a bug-watcher is probably a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges INSECTS IT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist is a researcher, someone whose job is to study things.

clue.text: He might be handy with an unusual book

definitions.text: He might be handy with an unusual book

parts.words: He might be handy with an unusual book
parts.note: handy hints at a handyman, while unusual gives odd and book the Old Testament Job

explanation.surface: A man who can fix things and who owns a strange volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius hints at the pieces in a loose way: 'unusual' is ODD, 'book' is the Book of Job, 'he' is the MAN, and 'handy' suggests a handyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-job man does small repair tasks, being practical and useful about the house.

clue.text: Writer reflected over first Greek letter

indicators.note: the reversed name sits over and around the next piece
a reflection shows a word back to front

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, English novelists
G for gold, the medal for first place

explanation.surface: An author looks back on the very first letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns AMIS into SIMA, which goes 'over' G (gold, first place) to give SIGMA. 'first Greek letter' tempts alpha; 'first' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth character of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to S.

clue.text: Tailors are not entirely involved in such matters

definitions.text: Tailors are not entirely involved in such matters

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order
the word before loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Tailors only partly take part in matters of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims ARE to AR; 'involved' rearranges TAILORS AR. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartorial means relating to tailoring or dress, exactly what tailors deal with.

clue.text: Customs are second matter in language of 1 across

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
1 across is a Latin motto, and res is Latin for thing or matter

explanation.surface: Customs officials discuss a second matter in a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is Latin, so 'language of 1 across' points to the Latin res. The answer is itself the Latin for customs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the customs and conventions of a community, a word borrowed from Latin.

clue.text: Indefinite article used in narration

indicators.note: indefinite means not fixed in form, so the letters are left loose to rearrange

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about using 'a' or 'an' when telling a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indefinite article' reads as grammar's 'a' or 'an'; 'Indefinite' rearranges ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is an account or telling of events, i.e. a narration.

clue.text: It gets you to sit up

definitions.text: It gets you to sit up

parts.words: It gets you to sit up
parts.note: reads as something that wakes you, but describes a seat that carries you up a mountain

explanation.surface: Something that makes you sit up and take notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairlift carries skiers seated up a slope, so you sit while going up.

clue.text: Padre, not a comic actor

indicators.note: says the following letter is left out

parts.note: a padre is a chaplain

explanation.surface: A clergyman insists he is not a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Chaplin was a silent-film comedian; 'not a' removes A from CHAPLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin is the famous silent-film comedian, an example of a comic actor.

clue.text: New man carries Old Labour leader or the opposite

indicators.note: the rearranged word holds the name within it
new means remade, so the letters of man are rearranged

parts.note: Tony Blair, a former leader of the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: A New Labour figure supports an Old Labour leader, or perhaps the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges MAN to ANM, which 'carries' TONY (Blair, a former Labour leader).
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning.

clue.text: Possibly a fish — an Iranian city?

indicators.note: says the letters may make something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a place in Iran is named after a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'an' look like the start of the definition, but it is the last piece; 'Possibly' rearranges only A FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Isfahan is a major city in central Iran, famous for its mosques.

clue.text: Hell's Angel sets off with it and puts the boot in sharp

definitions.text: Hell's Angel sets off with it

parts.note: puts the boot in means kicks
tart means sharp-tasting

explanation.surface: A biker starts his motorbike and lashes out with his boot.
explanation.walkthrough: Hell's Angels are bikers; older motorbikes were started by kicking a pedal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-start is the pedal used to start a motorcycle engine, which a biker uses to set off.

clue.text: Fish for rodent without offspring initially

parts.note: s.p. stands for sine prole, Latin for without offspring, used in family trees; 'initially' says to use its initials
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Fish offered to a rat that has no young.
explanation.walkthrough: In genealogy s.p. (sine prole, 'without issue') marks someone who died childless; 'initially' says the phrase is reduced to its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Tender of French metal

parts.note: fer is French for iron

explanation.surface: A bid of French iron.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to put forward, as an offer or bid.

clue.text: Alan Turing partly decoded and was not affected

indicators.note: decoding unscrambles a message, so these letters are put into a new order
only part of the word is used, its ending dropped

explanation.surface: Alan Turing cracked codes partly and was unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' cuts TURING to TUR; 'decoded' rearranges ALAN TUR. Turing was the British codebreaker of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural behaviour is unaffected, without pretence or artificiality.

clue.text: How Incitatus reportedly declined government office?

indicators.note: says the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: voted nay, refusing office: said no

explanation.surface: Wondering how Caligula's horse turned down the post of consul.
explanation.walkthrough: Incitatus was the Roman emperor Caligula's horse, said to have been made a consul; a horse would answer with a neigh.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's natural vocal response is a whinny, the sound Incitatus would make.

clue.text: Light-headed lady?

parts.note: light-headed reads as dizzy, but means a woman with very pale hair

explanation.surface: A woman feeling faint.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with silvery pale hair has a light-coloured head.
